items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1780

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to providing for elec-
tronic notarization

 
PURPOSE:

Allows for notarization to be done electronically with the use of video
conference technology.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the executive law by adding new section 137-a.  Defines
the terms "Electronic," "Electronic document," "Electronic notarial
act," "Electronic notary public," "Electronic notary," "Electronic
signature," "Electronic notarial statement of authority," "Notary elec-
tronic signature,"

Specifies the methods for identifying document signers for an electronic
notarization including video and for video and audio conference technol-
ogy sets standards for video and audio conference technology.

Sets forth registration requirements for electronic notaries public.
Establishes that any notarial act authorized by section 135 of this
article can be performed electronically. Sets forth instructions on how
electronic notarization is to be performed.

Section 2 provides that notaries public may collect fees for electronic
notarial services, as authorized by the Secretary of State

Section 3 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Every year, hundreds of millions of documents are notarized in the
United States: wills, mortgages, citizenship forms. Yet, despite the
increasing number of notarizations that occur annually, the industry has
not adapted to societal changes and technologic advance

Notarization still requires people to be physically present in front of
a notary public, despite new technology that would allow for the same
security over video and audio conference calls.

This legislation is not merely for convenience; Electronic Notorization
would allow homebound citizens to access notarial services and would
allow working people to have their documents notarized without losing
wages for lost working hours spent at an in-person notary public.

There are environmental benefits of Electronic Notarization as well as
it cuts down on paper usage.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020 - S435B Amend And Recommit to Environmental Conservation / Print
Number 4325A

Assembly 2020 - A7556A Amend And Recommit to Environmental Conservation
/ Print Number 7556A

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take 90 days after it becomes law.

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1780C

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to providing for elec-
tronic notarization

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Allows for notarization to be done electronically with the use of video
conference technology.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the executive law by adding new section 137-a. The bill
establishes definitions and sets forth registration requirements for
electronic notaries public. It establishes that notarial acts can be
performed electronically, subject to certain requirements. The bill also
sets forth instructions on how electronic notarization is to be
performed.

Section 2 provides that notaries public may collect fees for electronic
notarial services, as authorized by the Secretary of State.

Section 3 sets forth the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

The amended version of the bill establishes new consumer protection
requirements related to electronic notarizations.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Every year, hundreds of millions of documents are notarized in the
United States: wills, mortgages, citizenship forms. Yet, despite the
increasing number of notarizations that occur annually, the industry has
not adapted to societal changes and technologic advance Notarization
still requires people to be physically present in front of a notary
public, despite new technology that would allow for the same security
over video and audio conference calls.

This legislation is not merely for convenience; Electronic Notarization
would allow homebound citizens to access notarial services and would
allow working people to have their documents notarized without losing
wages for lost working hours spent at an in-person notary public.  There
are environmental benefits of Electronic Notarization as well as it cuts
down on paper usage.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: A4076B (Rozic) - Governmental Operations

2019: A4076A (Rozic) - Governmental Operations

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Minimal

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect 180 days after it shall have become a law.
Effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or repeal of any rule
or regulation necessary for the implementation of this act on its effec-
tive date are authorized to be made on or before such effective date.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 128 Chapter 767
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 1780-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the executive law, in relation to providing for
        electronic notarization"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would allow  licensed  notaries  to  perform  notarial  acts
through a complete, electronic format, also referred to as Remote Online
Notarization  (RON).  Under current law, notaries must be present at the
time they are  performing  these  notarial  acts.  During  the  COVID-19
pandemic,  Executive  Orders  allowed  notaries  to  perform  these acts
remotely, but they were still required to view the transaction and  they
were  required  to  physically sign the document. This is referred to as
Remote Ink Notary (RIN).

  While RIN is useful, it still required a notary to print off  a  docu-
ment  he or she received, sign that document, then scan or fax the docu-
ment back to the sender. This  current  bill,  which  authorizes  a  RON
system,  allows  all transactions to occur online. A notary receives the
document, signs it electronically, and can email it back to  the  sender
without ever having to print a paper copy.
 
  However,  according  to  the  bill,  prior to being able to use online
notarizations, a notary is required to register with the  Department  of
State.  Currently,  the  DOS  does  not have the ability to accept these
types of registrations. The Department needs to create a completely new,
online registration system. This process is  estimated  to  take  longer
than the six month effective date provided for in the bill.
 
  Therefore,  I  have  reached an agreement with the Legislature to pass
legislation in the upcoming session that will allow the DOS until  Janu-
ary  31, 2023 to create the necessary registration system. Additionally,
the Legislature has agreed to put a  RIN  system  in  place  during  the
pendency  of the registration system. This will allow notaries to under-
take the same remote procedures  that  they  took  during  the  pandemic
pursuant to Executive Order.
 
  On that basis, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
